papers.title: From Sky to Science: Time Domain Astronomy with the ILMT Survey
papers.abstract: The PyLMT transient detection pipeline has been operational since November 2023 and has detected $\sim$10,000 transients and variable objects in ILMT images in near real time. The survey has enabled the discovery and characterisation of a range of bright and faint optical transients. The detected population spans a broad diversity of astrophysical phenomena, including supernovae, variable stars, active galactic nuclei (AGN) variability, and Solar System objects such as asteroids and comets. We provide a concise overview of the detection of a variety of transient and variable classes identified with the ILMT, emphasising the survey's potential contributions to a broad class of astrophysical sources. We highlight representative science cases, including supernovae, AGNs, variable stars, and asteroids, to demonstrate the scientific potential of the ILMT survey.

papers.title: Occultation polarimetry as a probe of unresolved polarization
papers.abstract: Context: Low polarization in an unresolved source may reflect weak local polarization or spatial cancellation between strongly polarized regions. An occultation can break this spatial degeneracy by differentially sampling the source as the occulting boundary moves. Aims: We develop a general theoretical framework for occultation polarimetry and determine what information can be inferred directly from unresolved full Stokes light curves, without reconstructing a polarization image or prescribing a source model. Methods: For a stationary, spatially incoherent source undergoing monotonic occultation, we relate Stokes variations to the polarization sampled by an arbitrarily curved occulting boundary and derive an exact variance decomposition of the normalized Stokes vector. Results: The polarization deficit decomposes exactly into three non-negative contributions: local polarization deficit, mixing within limb samples, and mixing between their mean polarization states. The last is directly measurable and provides a sharp, model-independent lower bound on total spatial mixing. The associated covariance tensor further characterizes the direction and correlations of the resolved polarization variations, including those between linear and circular polarization. Finite sampling preserves the bound, which can be strengthened through complementary occultation trajectories. Conclusions: Occultation polarimetry provides a powerful observational technique for extracting quantitative, model independent constraints on spatial polarization mixing directly from unresolved Stokes light curves. It offers a means to reveal both the extent and the form of polarization structure otherwise inaccessible at the available angular resolution.

papers.title: The Long-Term Radial Velocity Stability of the COS G130M/1291 Mode
papers.abstract: We investigate the long-term radial velocity (RV) stability of one of the Far-UV (FUV) modes on the Cosmic Origins Spectrograph (COS). We do so by using a standard white dwarf, WD~0308-565, that has been observed over a large fraction of COS's operational lifetime of 17 years. We demonstrate that for modest signal-to-noise COS can return an RV stability of $<$3 km s$^{-1}$ over a baseline of 15 years. For higher SNR and a smaller number of epochs, we obtain $\sigma_{\mathrm V}=600$ m s$^{-1}$. We also show that the absolute radial velocity accuracy for this target is consistent with results from ground-based optical spectroscopy. We discuss some observational strategies and astrophysical objects that may be well suited to pushing to the very RV limit of the instrument. Utilizing COS for precision RV work opens a new scientific avenue for space-based UV astronomy as COS approaches 20 years of operations and hints at what may be possible with the stability of a high-resolution UV spectrograph on future missions such as the Habitable Worlds Observatory.

papers.title: A Spectroscopic Census of Cluster White Dwarfs from DESI, LAMOST, and SDSS
papers.abstract: Gaia has substantially expanded the sample of candidate white dwarfs (WDs) in open clusters, but many remain without spectroscopic characterization. We leverage the increasingly extensive archives of large public spectroscopic surveys to identify 62 candidate cluster WDs with available spectra from DESI, LAMOST, and SDSS. After discarding sources with very low S/N and unreliable host clusters, 44 candidates remain, including 37 non-magnetic DA WDs, of which 15 had not previously been characterized in the literature for cluster studies. We find that nine are consistent with single-star origins in their proposed host clusters, increasing the combined cluster DA initial--final mass relation (IFMR) sample to 132 WDs. All lie within $2\sigma$ of the best-fit IFMR from the most comprehensive recent cluster WD sample, suggesting these additions do not require recalibrating the empirical IFMR. One is a likely Hyades tidal-tail WD, providing further evidence that dynamical dispersal helps explain the long-standing WD deficit in the nearest cluster. We further compare WDs with spectra from multiple surveys. Among seven Praesepe WDs observed by both DESI and SDSS, DESI gives higher WD masses in six cases, with a mean difference of $0.067\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$, while the inferred progenitor masses differ by as much as $0.459\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. More broadly, nine of ten single-star cluster DAs with DESI spectra lie above the empirical IFMR, with a mean final-mass residual of $0.06\pm0.04\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. These results show that survey-dependent differences can strongly affect cluster WD parameters, and should be considered when combining heterogeneous spectroscopy in empirical IFMR studies.

papers.title: Mapping Wolf-Rayet winds with spectro-interferometry I. Detection of multiple co-rotating interaction regions in WR 6
papers.abstract: WR 6 is the prototype for periodic variability due to large-scale wind structures in Wolf-Rayet (WR) stars, showing a consistent periodicity of 3.76 d in photometry, spectroscopy, and polarimetry. However, the origin of this variability is debated, attributed either to corotating interaction regions (CIRs) or a low-mass companion. We use time-resolved interferometry to investigate the origin of periodic variability in WR 6. We aim to detect and characterize structures in the stellar winds of WR 6 and discriminate between the CIR and low-mass companion scenarios. Using the extended configuration of the Auxiliary Telescopes at VLTI, we obtained six GRAVITY epochs over six months to search for the presence and variability of wind-structures in WR 6. We also obtained complementary spectroscopic observations during one of the epochs to monitor contemporaneous spectral line variability. For all six epochs of GRAVITY observations: (i) WR 6 is consistent with a single star and has no spatially resolved companion detected above $M\gtrsim6\,M_\odot$; (ii) The He I line-emitting region is spatially resolved, while the He II lines remain unresolved, consistent with atmosphere models; (iii) Around 2.19 $\mu$m, discrete line-emitting features offset from the center of the star are detected. The number, positions, and wavelengths of these features vary across epochs. Spectroscopic monitoring reveals spectral line residuals that broadly correspond to the two features seen in the GRAVITY data of the fifth epoch. Finally, the first three epochs, observed on three consecutive nights, show significant variability in these features but cannot be directly linked across epochs. We thus report the detection of multiple large-scale structures in the wind of WR 6 with VLTI/GRAVITY. We favor CIRs as their likely origin owing to temporal and spatial variability that cannot be reconciled with a low-mass companion.

papers.title: An asteroseismic age estimate for the Pleiades using a neural-network emulator of rotating $\delta$ Scuti pulsation models
papers.abstract: Asteroseismology of $\delta$ Sct stars has strong potential for determining the ages of young stars through individual mode fitting. We present a neural-network emulator trained on approximately 46 million rotating pulsation models. From stellar mass, metallicity, age, and equatorial rotation velocity, it predicts 12 classical observables, two asteroseismic scalars, and the p mode, f mode and low-order g mode frequencies for degrees $\ell=0$-3, including the individual $m$ components of rotationally split multiplets. We couple the emulator to nested sampling through a multivariate likelihood that propagates correlated emulator residuals, making full Bayesian posterior exploration practical. Applied to five $\delta$ Sct stars in the Pleiades observed by TESS, the framework gives mutually consistent individual asteroseismic ages of 107-117 Myr. Combining their age posteriors gives a cluster age of $113.3\pm4.5$ Myr (statistical), consistent with the $112 \pm 5$ Myr lithium-depletion-boundary age and the 110-160 Myr range from rotating-isochrone fitting. Together with spectroscopic $v\sin i$, the inferred equatorial velocities also provide post-fit inclination estimates. Separate perturbed-grid tests using 100 matched synthetic pairs per input-physics variation give median absolute age shifts of $2.1$, $2.3$, and $5.2$ Myr for $|\Delta f_{\rm ov}|=0.005$, $|\Delta\alpha_{\rm MLT}|=0.1$, and $|\Delta Y|=0.02$, respectively; the corresponding 90th percentile shifts are $6.5$, $7.6$, and $16.2$ Myr. These tests describe conditional population sensitivities, not a systematic uncertainty on the Pleiades age. Together, the cluster-age agreement and the scale of these input-physics sensitivities support $\delta$ Sct asteroseismology as a complementary age estimation method for young stars.

papers.title: Aditya-L1 and SDO Observations of a Confined X-Class Flare with an EUV Late Phase: Thermal and Nonthermal Emission, Magnetic Topology, and Flux Rope Confinement
papers.abstract: We study a long-duration, confined X2.0-class solar flare exhibiting three distinct episodes of HXR emission, along with an accompanying EUV late phase. A key highlight of this work is the novel observations from the high-resolution solar X-ray spectrometers SoLEXS and HEL1OS onboard Aditya-L1, providing insights into the evolution of thermal and non-thermal emissions. Simultaneous EUV observations from AIA/SDO in hot channels, combined with multi-band X-ray light curves, reveal a two-stage confined eruption of a large MFR, separated by $\sim$10~minutes. The first stage corresponds to an M4.6 flare, while the overall event reaches X2.0 on the GOES scale. During the first phase, magnetic reconnection beneath the large EUV hot channel causes plasma heating to $\sim$19~MK, with a non-thermal spectral index of $\sim$4.3. In the second phase, characterized by external reconnection and confinement of the MFR hot channel, the temperature increases to $\sim$22~MK, accompanied by further hardening of the spectral index to $\sim$3.9. Despite pronounced non-thermal signatures and enhanced particle acceleration, the MFR fails to erupt through the overlying coronal loops because of the strong strapping force exerted by the large overlying coronal loops. Importantly, the stalled eruption, together with reconnection in the higher overlying loops, results in enhanced heating within a closed magnetic configuration, with temperatures peaking at up to $\sim$15~MK during the late phase. The paper also provides the first observations of detectable non-thermal X-ray emission during the early EUV late phase, albeit briefly, providing direct evidence for reconnection-induced heating, likely occurring in the higher overlying coronal loops.

papers.title: TESS flares and chromospheric variability in the Pleiades, the Hyades, and Praesepe
papers.abstract: Magnetic activity is a result of the interaction between rotation and dynamo processes in cool stars with outer convection zones. Since open cluster members share a common age, distance, and chemical composition, they provide an opportunity to study the magnetic activity of cool stars in a controlled astrophysical context. We used 120s cadence observations from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) to study the flare activity of stars in three open clusters with different ages: the Pleiades (100 Myr), the Hyades (700 Myr) and Praesepe (700 Myr). We used the Ohio State Multi-Object Spectrograph (OSMOS) at MDM Observatory with the goal of identifying coronal mass ejections (CMEs) in the Pleiades and Praesepe. We investigated the flaring characteristics of the cluster members using the TESS light curves: we identified the flares, then divided the dataset into different categories based on the effective temperature and light curve amplitude. We calculated the flare energies and investigated the flare frequency distributions. We studied the dynamic spectra of the H$\alpha$ line and its environment to search for indication of CMEs. The power-law indices of the flare frequency distributions obtained in our analysis span the 1.8-2.8 range. We found the highest flare rates in the Pleiades for all investigated spectral types. Our results show that the flare rate of M dwarfs is similar in the Pleiades and the Hyades while for K-type stars the flare rate in the Pleiades is an order of magnitude higher. Our analysis reveals that the flare rate in M stars changes with their effective temperature: the rate is highest for T$_{eff}$ $\sim$3200-3300 K -coinciding with the transition between partially and fully convective stars - with smooth decrease in flare rate towards cooler and hotter M dwarfs. We used the MDM/OSMOS spectra to place an upper limit on the CME rate.

papers.title: The nearby Type II supernova 2024ggi beyond 600 days: circumstellar interaction and dust formation
papers.abstract: The Type II SN 2024ggi is one of the nearest core-collapse SNe to have exploded in recent decades. Its proximity has enabled extensive multiwavelength monitoring from early times through the nebular phase. Signatures of late-time interaction between the SN ejecta and hydrogen-rich circumstellar material (CSM) have recently been reported. Here we extend its study using late-time optical photometry and spectroscopy from 570 to 820 d after explosion. We investigate the emergence and evolution of late-time ejecta-CSM interaction and constrain the geometry of the interaction region and the properties of newly formed dust. Comparisons with other interacting SNe II and with synthetic spectra are presented. We model the H$\alpha$ profile with the Monte Carlo radiative-transfer code Damocles, including both gas and dust components. Spectroscopic signatures of interaction precede the photometric flattening. The spectra evolve from ejecta-dominated to interaction-dominated as H$\alpha$ develops a broad, boxy profile. The optical light curves subsequently flatten relative to the $^{56}$Co decay rate at approximately 650-670 d. The emission lines show a systematic blue-to-red asymmetry that requires a dust component newly formed within the ejecta. The inferred dust mass formed in the ejecta is $10^{-6}-10^{-5}$ M$_\odot$ if the grains are amorphous carbon or a carbon-silicate mixture, but can reach up to $10^{-3}$ M$_\odot$ for pure silicates.

papers.title: An upper limit on Galactic OB+black hole binaries from SDSS-V
papers.abstract: Binaries composed of a luminous OB star and a black hole (BH) are a key evolutionary link between massive stellar binaries and merging compact-object binaries, but only a handful are known and their occurrence fraction remains poorly constrained. We use multi-epoch spectroscopy from the SDSS-V Milky Way Mapper to place a first rigorous empirical upper limit on the fraction of Galactic massive ($\geq 10\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) OB stars with a close BH companion, $f_\mathrm{BH}$. Radial-velocity (RV) variability alone cannot distinguish BH companions from the far more numerous luminous binaries. We therefore combine the SDSS-V RV variability measurements of 3130 massive OB stars with high-resolution follow-up and literature information to identify luminous companions among the RV-variable subset. Forward-modelling the detectability of OB+BH systems using BH masses and orbital parameters from binary-evolution models, we find $f_\mathrm{BH} \lesssim 3\%$ at 95% credibility. This empirical upper limit approaches, but does not exclude, theoretical predictions for the OB+BH fraction. The constraint is primarily limited by the number of RV-variable systems that can be decisively classified, highlighting the importance of complete, high-quality follow-up for future searches.

papers.title: What Does 2D Coronal Seismology Measure?
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) coronal seismology based on coronagraphic imaging spectroscopy has emerged as a promising method for mapping the coronal magnetic field, but the physical meaning of its inferred quantities under optically thin line-of-sight (LOS) integration remains uncertain. We investigate this problem by synthesizing coronagraphic observables from a global wave-driven magnetohydrodynamic model with a long LOS extent and a structured corona, and by applying the same analysis procedures used for observations. We compare the diagnosed density, wave propagation direction, phase speed, and magnetic-field strength with different LOS-weighted reference quantities from the model. We find that the measured density and the wave propagation direction are both well represented by LOS emissivity-weighted quantities. In contrast, the phase speed is not controlled by emissivity weighting alone: the LOS distribution of wave velocity amplitude also plays an important role. As a result, the inferred magnetic field is better represented by combining the emissivity-weighted density with an amplitude-dependent effective speed. Emissivity weighting nevertheless remains a reasonable approximation, and a useful baseline, over much of the field of view, especially where the LOS does not cross strongly structured plasma-sheet-like regions. These results clarify the physical interpretation of 2D coronal seismology and provide guidance for future coronal magnetic-field tomography and model-constrained applications.

papers.title: Star spots mimic the proposed abundance signatures of planet formation
papers.abstract: Trends with stellar elemental abundances and condensation temperature have been proposed as a possible tracer of rocky planet formation. Here we present an alternative explanation, where we show that stellar activity (star spots) can also cause apparent abundance changes in refractory elements preferentially over volatile elements. This effect arises naturally from atomic physics: refractory (rocky; high-$T_c$) elements preferentially have low first-ionization potentials, with strong transitions that are most sensitive to the cooler, magnetically-perturbed spot conditions, making any spot-induced change in line strength correlated with $T_c$. We re-examine literature on Sun-like stars in the Solar neighborhood and find that the $\log{R'_{HK}}$ stellar activity indicator is correlated with the so-called $T_c$ slope: the gradient of chemical abundances with respect to condensation temperature. Using 1D LTE Korg.jl simulations of the Sun with spots of varying size and contrast, we show that a wide range of spot configurations can manifest as abundance patterns that mimic a signal of abundance trends with condensation temperature. Finally, we conduct a line-by-line differential analysis of an ambient Solar spectrum relative to a Solar sunspot umbra to represent an extreme case, where we find that elements with high condensation temperature can show a factor of three (0.5 dex) increase. We discuss implications that stellar activity poses for precision spectroscopy, and provide some direction on how this effect might be mitigated.

papers.title: Photometric and Spectroscopic Observations of Comet 2P/Encke's Nucleus in the Mid-Infrared Wavelength Region
papers.abstract: We observed comet 2P/Encke with the Cooled Mid-Infrared Camera and Spectrometer (COMICS) on the Subaru telescope on UT 2003 November 12.3, when the comet was at heliocentric and geocentric distances of 1.09 and 0.27 au, respectively. Imaging observations of the comet with narrow-band filters centered at 8.8, 10.5, 11.7, 12.4, 18.8, and 24.5 $\mu$m and low-resolution spectroscopic observations in the N-band (8-13 $\mu$m, $R\sim250$) of the comet were performed. The observed spatial profiles of the comet were consistent with those of a standard star (FWHM $\sim$ 0.3'' at 10.5 $\mu$m, close to the diffraction-limited image size), indicating that the observed spectrum was dominated by thermal emission from the cometary nucleus. The semi-axial ratio ($a$/$b$) of the nucleus of 2P/Encke is estimated as 2.26$^{+0.33}_{-0.21}$ based on the isothermal, prolate ellipsoid model. The photometric data with the correction for rotational phases, can be explained by a blackbody temperature of $328\pm7$ K, consistent with the nucleus surface temperature empirically estimated at 1.09 au from the Sun (327 K). This blackbody approximation for the nucleus leads to $a = 3.6^{+0.5}_{-0.3}$ km and $b = 1.6^{+0.2}_{-0.2}$ km by assuming an emissivity of unity. The observed low-resolution N-band spectrum showed an overall smooth continuum with no prominent excess emission feature at $\sim$10 $\mu$m due to fine silicate grains in the cometary coma. The relative emissivity spectrum of the nucleus showed a negative feature at $\sim$9.5 $\mu$m, as seen in the mid-infrared nucleus spectrum of 460P/PanSTARRS [T. Ootsubo, et al. (2021), Icarus, 363, 114425].

papers.title: High-resolution transmission spectroscopy of KELT-18b Metastable helium detection at 1083 nm
papers.abstract: We present the first high-resolution transmission spectroscopy of the ultrahot Jupiter KELT-18b, probing its escaping atmosphere by analyzing a single transit obtained with the CARMENES spectrograph. Transmission spectroscopy and Doppler tomography were utilized to isolate the planetary signal. To mitigate contamination from the strong telluric OH lines overlapping the region of interest, two distinct data analysis procedures were applied: a standard Molecfit and OH-masking approach as well as a PCA-based method. By combining the two complementary approaches, we successfully detect a He\,I triplet absorption feature of $1.10 \pm 0.22\%$ ($5.1\sigma$). The signal exhibits a velocity shift consistent with zero and is attributed to the exoplanetary atmosphere. An injection test reveals that the PCA-based method significantly suppresses the retrieved signal. Additionally, using the ATES and TPM codes, we modeled the atmospheric photoevaporation and the helium triplet profile for different He/H ratios and stellar XUV fluxes, accounting for instrument and planetary rotational broadening. From our simulations we derive a mass-loss rate and an evaporation efficiency for KELT-18b of $10.47 \leq \log_{10}(\dot{M}) \leq 11.68$ and $0.153 \leq \eta \leq 0.321$, demonstrating that the atmosphere of KELT-18b is undergoing photoevaporation. Furthermore, our simulations show good agreement with the observed transmission spectrum, allowing us to exclude very low He/H ratios at a $3\sigma$ confidence level for XUV fluxes up to approximately twice the nominal reconstructed value. Our result expands the known parameter space of exoplanets with confirmed helium absorption, establishing KELT-18b as the most massive planet orbiting the hottest host star with such a detection.

papers.title: Size, atmospheric, and ring constraints on the large Kuiper belt object (55565) Aya from a stellar occultation
papers.abstract: We aim to constrain the projected size, geometric albedo, possible atmosphere, and possible ring material of the mid-sized trans-Neptunian object (55565) Aya from the stellar occultation of 2024 May 10 (UT). We observed the event from three Japanese sites with high-cadence optical imaging. We combined one positive occultation chord with an informative prior on the shadow centre derived from orbital and astrometric uncertainties, and inferred the body radius with Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo modelling. We constrained a possible atmosphere by fitting refraction models for pure CH$_4$, N$_2$, and CO atmospheres to multi-band light curves, and searched for ring-like extinction signatures in unbinned and binned high-time-resolution photometry. We derive an equivalent radius, i.e., the radius of the circle fitted to the projected shadow, of $r=401^{+28}_{-40}$ km for Aya, corresponding to a geometric albedo of $p_V=0.101^{+0.023}_{-0.013}$. This estimate is insensitive to the adopted ephemeris solution and is consistent with an ephemeris-independent analysis that makes no assumption about the position of the shadow centre. We obtain 3$\sigma$ upper limits on the atmospheric surface pressure of $p_0=60$, 90, and 80 nbar for pure CH$_4$, N$_2$, and CO compositions, respectively. No significant ring-like extinction is detected over projected distances of about 430-8060 km sampled by the three stations, and our most sensitive data exclude dense narrow features with apparent opacity $p'\gtrsim0.1$ and radial widths of a few kilometres or larger over $\sim3r$-$14r$. This is the first stellar occultation by Aya ever observed. In addition to constraining Aya's size and albedo and finding no ring-like extinction, we place a stringent atmospheric upper limit that supports diversity in atmospheric states among similarly sized trans-Neptunian objects.

papers.title: Physical characterization of Earth's quasi-satellite 2025 PN7
papers.abstract: A hypothetical origin as lunar ejecta for Earth's quasi-satellites (QS) has gained initial support in recent years, but there is scarce photometric and/or spectroscopic data to support the premise due to the rare observational windows to obtain such data for these small objects. One of the key pieces of evidence supporting the lunar-origin hypothesis, the lunar-like, very red reflectance spectrum of QS (469219) Kamo'oalewa, was recently found to be flawed. We present reflectance spectroscopy of Earth's QS 2025~PN$_7$ obtained with FORS2 at UT1-Antu of the ESO Very Large Telescope. This is only the second QS that has ever been characterized, the first being (469219) Kamo'oalewa, the sample-return target of the Tianwen-2 mission. Our results indicate that 2025~PN$_7$ exhibits a near-solar, flat visual spectrum, most consistent with the B-type in the Bus-DeMeo taxonomy. Our results therefore still support an asteroid-belt origin for most of Earth's QSs. The lunar-ejecta hypothesis can only be formally rejected with a larger sample of spectroscopically characterized QSs.

papers.title: A Spatial Map of the Atmospheric Limb of a Hot Jupiter
papers.abstract: Planets are inherently three-dimensional objects shaped by their thermal structure and dynamics. Observations of transiting exoplanets have begun to uncover this three-dimensional nature, with JWST measuring their dayside atmosphere structure with eclipse mapping, and exploring spectroscopic asymmetries in the limbs of planets during transit. We apply the novel mapping method of transmission strings to the hot Jupiter WASP-17b. With this method, we are not only able to extract hemispheric limb asymmetries from east-to-west, but can map equator-to-pole variations around the transmitting atmosphere as a function of angle, spanning 0.6-12$\mu$m. We find a clear transition in the thermal scale height around the limb of the atmosphere, with a $\sim$650K temperature difference between the morning (T=858$^{+434}_{-233}$K) and evening (T=1522$^{+116}_{-114}$K). These results are consistent with both nightside emission and dayside eclipse mapping measurements, and represent a fully comprehensive set of observations for a transiting exoplanet. We are also able to constrain the abundances of H$_2$O and CO$_2$ to constant values around the limb, providing observational constraints to results from global circulation models. The transmission string technique combined with the outstanding observability of WASP-17b pushes the study of exoplanet atmospheres further into a three-dimensional understanding of hot Jupiter dynamics and chemistry

papers.title: What does self-supervision add to engineered features for stellar light curves?
papers.abstract: TESS light curves encode a star's pulsation, rotation, binarity and oscillations, among other physical properties, but the survey produces far more light curves than can be labelled by hand. Astronomers have engineered a few dozen physically motivated features from them, which together remain a strong baseline. Previous work has trained encoders on light curves and judged them by their own downstream scores, but has not asked what they add to the engineered features. We pre-train a convolutional encoder on unlabelled TESS light curves to predict each window's latent representation from those of its neighbours. We then freeze it, add its features to the 25 engineered features, and read the combination out with one fixed linear probe on ten tasks: five variability classes, four asteroseismic targets and rotation period. Adding the learned features improves the readout on 7 of 10 tasks over the engineered features alone, where an untrained encoder does not. The combination also outperforms two networks trained end-to-end on the same labelled stars on most tasks. An encoder trained without labels therefore gives astronomers new features that complement the ones they already use rather than replace them.

papers.title: A Quest for Changing-State AGNs
papers.abstract: We use Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) light curves to identify photometrically selected changing-state active galactic nucleus (CSAGN) candidates. We employ unsupervised deep learning and anomaly detection methods to identify unusual patterns of variability in the light curves of 872,228 AGNs with known variability. We find that 8,504 light curves show anomalous behavior. Among these, 682 sources show evidence for two-state photometric behavior during the Gaia DR3 observing baseline. These 682 CSAGN candidates were selected using an automated statistical pattern recognition approach based on Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) to identify sources whose magnitude distributions are consistent with two preferred brightness levels, substantially reducing the need for human visual inspection in selecting the CSAGN candidates. The candidates tend to have fainter absolute magnitudes and lower redshifts than the non-anomalous Gaia variable AGN sample, suggesting that some may be accreting at lower rates. Our approach builds a large candidate sample with less reliance on human visual selection. Follow-up observations of these sources can help identify what drives changing-state transitions and clarify their connection to accretion-disk physics and supermassive black hole (SMBH) fueling.

papers.title: Ultraviolet Reflected-Light Spectroscopy of Modern Earth Analogs with Starshade Observations
papers.abstract: Characterizing rocky, habitable zone planets in reflected light is a key science objective for future direct imaging missions, and the ultraviolet (UV) is uniquely suited for supporting the characterization of Earth-like atmospheres. The Hartley-Huggins ozone band at $0.25 ~\mu\mathrm{m}$ remains detectable at low spectral resolution down to $0.1\%$ PAL $\mathrm{O}_2$, providing a sensitive proxy for oxygen-bearing chemistry even for Proterozoic-like atmospheres where the visible and near-infrared $\mathrm{O}_2$ features become inaccessible. This work uses an end-to-end framework for UV starshade spectroscopy of modern Earth analogs that integrates high-fidelity observation simulation, conservative post-processing, and Bayesian spectral retrieval to quantify ozone detection significance. The framework is applied across 108 simulated scenes spanning a range of planet phase angles, system inclinations, and exozodiacal dust densities. The results establish that robust ozone detection with UV-only, $R=7$ reflected light spectroscopy requires a photometric $\mathrm{SNR} \sim 30$. UV starshade observations with the Habitable Worlds Observatory achieve this threshold within 3-day integrations for solar-type systems at 10 parsecs with inclinations up to $60^\circ$ at favorable phases ($\leq 90^\circ$). Above this SNR threshold, ozone detections are robust to systematic bias from imperfect exozodi calibration within $\sim30\%$, and the median retrieved ozone abundance remains accurate to within one order of magnitude of the true value.

papers.title: Elastic Properties of Titan Tholins Revealed by Brillouin Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Titan tholins, complex organic solids synthesized by simulating photochemical processes in Titan's atmosphere, are widely regarded as analogs to organic surface materials on the Saturnian moon. Their mechanical properties are critical for understanding the evolution of Titan's geomorphology and crustal layering. Here, we report the first direct experimental determination of the complete set of aggregate elastic moduli of tholins using Brillouin spectroscopy. Measurements conducted on tholin powder samples yielded a bulk modulus of 11 (2) GPa and a shear modulus of 3.9 (5) GPa, from which we derive a Young's modulus of 11 (1) GPa and a Poisson's ratio of 0.34 (3). Thin-film samples synthesized under slightly different conditions yield similar results. Compared with other Titan-relevant organic compounds, tholins exhibit the highest elastic stiffness measured to date, exceeding even H2O ice in both bulk and shear moduli. These results support the interpretation that complex organics contribute significantly to the mechanical stability and transport behavior of Titan's equatorial dune sediments. Measurements following prolonged atmospheric exposure reveal persistent stiffening of tholins that remains after vacuum treatment, likely associated with minor chemical modification and physical reorganization, highlighting the importance of controlled sample handling for future laboratory investigations. This study also demonstrates the effectiveness of Brillouin spectroscopy as a non-destructive technique for characterizing planetary organic materials and provides new constraints relevant to future seismic and geophysical investigations by the Dragonfly mission.

papers.title: Simulating Ionospheric Distortions in Mock SKA-Low Solar Radio Observations
papers.abstract: The Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) will provide unprecedented angular resolution for low-frequency solar radio imaging, enabling access to fine-scale coronal structures. However, the improved spatial resolution of SKA-Low also increases the sensitivity of solar images to ionospheric propagation effects. We investigate the impact of ionospheric fluctuations on simulated SKA-Low solar observations at 50, 100, 150, and 200 MHz using the \textsc{Karabo} simulator and turbulent, moving ionospheric phase screens. We quantify the resulting image distortions using spatial power spectral density (PSD) analysis and compare the SKA response with corresponding MWA simulations. The results show that ionospheric distortions are strongly scale- and frequency-dependent, with the maximum fractional PSD distortion decreasing with observing frequencies. SKA resolves ionospheric fluctuations over spatial scales that are largely smoothed by the MWA instrumental response, with significant distortions occurring on scales comparable to solar active-region structures. These results demonstrate that ionospheric propagation effects should be considered when interpreting high-resolution SKA-low solar radio images, particularly at the lower end of the frequency band.

papers.title: The EBLM project - XX. Absolute dynamical masses of five low-mass eclipsing binaries, and an evaluation of mass estimation methods
papers.abstract: Eclipsing binaries consisting of a solar-type primary and an M dwarf secondary are key laboratories to study objects at the bottom of the main sequence. Fundamental parameters of such stars have a direct impact upon exoplanetary studies, as searches for temperate Earth-sized planets focus on M dwarf hosts. Eclipsing binaries are essential to measure these parameters. However for stellar masses $<$ 0.35 M$_\odot$ , few double-lined eclipsing systems are known. Thus, stellar evolution models and empirical relations have had to rely on single-lined eclipsing binaries, for instance those from the EBLM project (Eclipsing Binary - Low Mass). Using high resolution spectroscopy to extract the weak signal of the secondary (flux ratio $<$ 1 per cent in the optical), we transform five more systems from single to double-lined, deriving absolute masses for both stars. We then compare methods typically employed to estimate stellar masses for field stars or single-lined binaries with the absolute dynamical masses we obtain, to assess their accuracy. Our results for SB1 and SB2 analyses are mostly consistent within 1-$\sigma$, though we identify a small systematic overestimation of SB1 masses derived from a combination of radial velocities and eclipse photometry. We show that the bias originates from primary radius overestimation during isochronal analysis, wherein the secondary light reduces photometric magnitudes and impacts the recovered radii by modifying the spectral energy distribution. With proper calibration, we can ensure the accuracy of using the full EBLM SB1 sample to constrain mass-radius-luminosity relationships for the smallest, yet most abundant, stars in the Galaxy

papers.title: Reawakening of GS 1843+00: A Multiwavelength Study of its 2026 Giant X-ray Outburst
papers.abstract: GS 1843+00 (Ginga 1843+009) is a poorly studied Be/X-ray binary system that underwent a major X-ray outburst in 2026 February-May after nearly sixteen years of quiescence. We present an X-ray, optical, and radio study of GS 1843+00 during this outburst, focusing on the evolution of the neutron star emission geometry, Be-disk connection, and possible outflow activity. We analyse three NuSTAR observations obtained at different stages of the outburst, complemented by archival RXTE and Chandra data, optical spectroscopy and imaging with the Nordic Optical Telescope, and a MeerKAT radio observation. NuSTAR observations reveal coherent X-ray pulsations around 29.7 s with a spin-up rate of $(-5.1\pm0.1)\times10^{-8}$ s s$^{-1}$ during the outburst. The pulse profiles show strong evolution with energy and outburst phase, with distinct morphologies even at comparable luminosities. The pulsed fraction varies between 1 and 16% and exhibits a complex reversal in energy dependence above 7 keV, increasing with energy during the first two observations and decreasing during the third. The 3-79 keV broadband spectra are described by thermal Comptonization with a blackbody and an Fe K$\alpha$ emission line, with no evidence for a cyclotron absorption feature. Phase-resolved spectroscopy reveals variations in the Comptonization and blackbody parameters, indicating changes in the accretion-column structure. Optical spectroscopy confirms the presence of a Be-circumstellar disk through H$\alpha$ and Paschen-series emission lines. No radio counterpart is detected, with a $3\sigma$ upper limit of 36 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ at 1.28 GHz. Weaker H$\alpha$ emission compared with previous epochs indicates that the Be-circumstellar disk was in a different state during the current episode, while the radio non-detection suggests that any associated outflow activity was faint or below the detection limit.

papers.title: Blackbody evolution and circumstellar medium properties of broad-lined H-rich superluminous supernovae
papers.abstract: Broad-lined H-rich superluminous supernovae (SLSNe II) tend to show signs of interaction, including a UV excess compared to a blackbody function. However, a quantitative analysis of the CSM configuration and the UV excess has so far not been performed for most of the literature sample. Additionally, SN 2023gpw showed signs of asymmetry in its peculiar blackbody and spectral evolution, raising the question of whether similar properties can be found in other SLSNe II. We aim to characterize the circumstellar environment of SLSNe II by searching for signs of asymmetry, quantifying the UV excess, and investigating any IR echoes produced by dust. Diversity among SLSNe II is also explored. We fit blackbody functions to the SEDs of SLSNe II to quantify the UV excess luminosity and its evolution. We use this to investigate mass-loss rates required to produce the excess through interaction. We also investigate the line profiles in SLSN II at late times and compare line velocities to the blackbody radius evolution. We examine public WISE IR images and place constraints on IR echoes. We find mass loss rates of $\sim10^{-4}$ to $\sim0.03\, \mathrm{M_\odot}$~yr$^{-1}$ when assuming all interaction luminosity emerges in the UV, i.e., conservative lower limits for the total mass loss rate. Radii calculated from line velocities in late-time spectra are mostly too large for a spherical interaction photosphere, only compatible with the blackbody radius evolution if the CSM is non-spherical with a low filling factor. This is in some cases supported by a mismatch between spectroscopic and blackbody expansion velocities. Considerable diversity is seen in the sample, probably as a result of different viewing angles and CSM masses. WISE images seem too shallow to observe IR echoes in SLSNe II beyond $z\sim0.1$, but in the nearest event, SN 2020jhm, a likely IR echo is detected, suggesting pre-existing dust.

papers.title: Dynamically Coupled Three-dimensional Cloud-Chemistry in Rapidly Rotating Irradiated Atmospheres: an Application to the Compact White Dwarf-Brown Dwarf system ZTFJ0038+2030
papers.abstract: Clouds and disequilibrium chemistry shape the observable properties of substellar and planetary atmospheres, and JWST time-resolved spectroscopy now enables direct tests of their three-dimensional structures. We present an update to the 3D atmospheric framework ADAM, coupling the dynamical core to a miniature kinetic chemistry scheme (mini-chem) and a saturation-relaxation tracer cloud module. Using this framework, we investigate the atmosphere of the brown dwarf orbiting the white dwarf ZTFJ0038+2030 in a 10-hour orbit. The brown dwarf receives stellar irradiation comparable to its internal heat flux, placing the atmosphere in a regime where the circulation is characterized by a standing Matsuno--Gill wave response and equatorial superrotation. Rapid rotation confines these structures closer to the equator, producing more symmetric broadband light curves with smaller hotspot offsets than canonical hot Jupiters, in agreement with recent JWST observations of this system. Although most species are globally homogenized, rapid rotation limits global-scale horizontal mixing and allows circulation-driven vertical transport to maintain strong CO and CO$_2$ inhomogeneities in the photosphere. These chemical inhomogeneities produce asymmetric phase curves in the CO and CO$_2$ absorption bands, which could qualitatively explain the observed CO$_2$ light-curve asymmetry. When clouds are included, Na$_2$S clouds dominate the photosphere and weaken the large-scale circulation, lowering photospheric CO and CO$_2$ abundances, while MgSiO$_3$ and Fe clouds rain out at deeper levels. Because the dominant Na$_2$S clouds reside mostly above the quench region, cloud-driven convection has limited impact on the quenched abundances, which are instead regulated mainly by large-scale circulation.

papers.title: Harmonic and intermodulation emission from direct-to-device satellites - Harmonics of the Starlink 2.6 GHz downlink and the products around them
papers.abstract: Direct-to-device (DTD) satellites carry mobile base stations transmitting in terrestrial mobile bands. Their non-linear emission products can fall into radio astronomy bands, including passive bands. We measure the harmonics of the Starlink DTD downlink at 2620-2630 MHz and the intermodulation products around them, search for products next to the carriers, and compare them with the ITU-R unwanted-emission limits and radio astronomy protection criteria. We use autocorrelations of single Australia Telescope Compact Array antennas on tracked passes of DTD and other satellites with the 16 cm and 4 cm receivers. Harmonic ratios and receiver tests show that the harmonics are satellite-generated. We simulate the aggregate equivalent power flux density of a constellation at Effelsberg and the ATCA. The harmonics H2 to H4 at 5240, 7860 and 10480 MHz fall by about 16 dB per order, show no trend with elevation, and originate on the satellite. H2 is also detected in 32% of integrations more than 10 degrees from any DTD satellite. Inside the harmonic zones the spectra follow the n-fold convolution of the carriers; outside them, intermodulation products of order n+2 and higher lie on average 19 dB below the zone and switch between -23 and -15 dB within seconds. Next to the carriers no satellite emission is detected to 33 dB below the carriers. H2, >=-38.9 dBW in 4 kHz isotropic-equivalent, is at or above the SM.329 space-station limit; H3 and H4 meet it. For 8640 satellites the aggregate exceeds the protection criteria by 65 and 25 dB at the second and fifth harmonics, and by >100 dB for out-of-band emission at the mask level in 2690-2700 MHz. Harmonics are received far outside the serving beams. Their radiated level must be limited directly, not through the power at the antenna port. Compliance with per-satellite ITU-R limits does not protect radio astronomy from the aggregate of a constellation.

papers.title: ELISA: A Bayesian X/$\gamma$-ray Spectral Analysis Toolkit
papers.abstract: Forward-folded X/$\gamma$-ray spectral fitting increasingly benefits from Bayesian workflows to better capture counting statistics, background uncertainties, and complex parameter degeneracies, while fully reproducible end-to-end implementations are still not always straightforward to deploy in routine analyses. We present ELISA (Efficient Library for Spectral Analysis), an open-source Python toolkit that streamlines the full spectral analysis loop for X/$\gamma$-ray astronomy: data loading, model construction, inference, and model validation and comparison. ELISA couples a JAX-accelerated forward model with a unified fitting interface, supporting both rapid optimization and modern Bayesian sampling. Built-in diagnostics make convergence checks and predictive assessment a standard part of the workflow, motivating principled model refinement when needed. Using a spectral fitting example of the Insight-HXMT Crab observation, we find substantial improvements in sampling efficiency compared with XSPEC's default MCMC implementation. ELISA is available at https://github.com/wcxve/elisa and on PyPI at https://pypi.org/project/astro-elisa.

papers.title: Mid-IR Water-Vapor Seeing: Implications for ELT/METIS High-Contrast Imaging from VLTI Data
papers.abstract: Direct imaging and characterization of rocky exoplanets remains one of the central challenges in exoplanetary science. The mid-infrared (mid-IR) offers a favorable high-contrast imaging (HCI) regime, as the planet-star contrast is more moderate than at shorter wavelengths. However, mid-IR observations with extremely large ground-based telescopes (ELTs) are strongly affected by spatio-temporal fluctuations in atmospheric water vapor (WV), which introduce chromatic wavefront errors that are largely invisible to adaptive optics systems operating at shorter wavelengths. This poses a significant challenge for mid-IR HCI instruments such as METIS, which aims to detect thermal emission from rocky exoplanets in the $N$-band (8--13 $\mu$ m). To quantify WV-induced wavefront errors, we analyze $K$-band fringe-tracker data from the GRAVITY instrument at the VLTI and derive the optical path difference between group-delay and phase-delay measurements. This difference provides a direct measure of the differential WV column density ($\Sigma$) above the telescopes. We examine the dependence of the RMS differential WV column density ($\sigma_{\Sigma}$) on precipitable water vapor (PWV), airmass, seeing, and wind speed across multiple VLTI configurations. Among these parameters, PWV shows the strongest correlation with $\sigma_{\Sigma}$. We further explore the influence of the vertical PWV distribution on this relationship. Next, we use power-spectral-density analysis to quantify how increasing PWV modulates $\Sigma$ variability. The wavefront error associated with this phenomenon on ELT scale is approximately 15~nm RMS in the $L$-band and 175~nm RMS in the $N$-band, relative to the $K$-band. These results provide a quantitative framework for assessing and mitigating atmospheric WV effects in next-generation mid-IR HCI instruments.

papers.title: Modelling the Point Spread Function of ILMT images
papers.abstract: We have devised an approach to model the empirical Point Spread Function (PSF) of the images taken with the 4-meter International Liquid Mirror Telescope (ILMT). The characteristics of the ILMT PSF are influenced by the nature of the Liquid Mirror, as well as by instrument specific and atmospheric factors. As the telescope uses Time Delay Integration (TDI) mode for tracking the passing objects, the PSF varies along the declination axis due to differential motion and star-trail curvature. The 5-element optical corrector homogenizes the PSF to some degree, but does not completely eliminate the disturbing effects mentioned above. The PSF in the RA direction is changing due to the sky conditions. We show that we can successfully model the PSF of 4k$\times$4k chunks using PSFEx, accounting for second-order X-Y variability. Our software robustly reproduces the PSF and its variation across the field.

papers.title: The Simons Observatory: Frequency-resolved beam calibration for the SO SATs with POLOCALC
papers.abstract: We present a far-field beam calibration of the Simons Observatory (SO) Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs) using scanned single-frequency measurements of a drone-mounted source emitting in the 90 GHz band, where the SATs have an angular resolution of $\sim$30$'$. We then compare the results from two campaigns in April and December 2025 to the band-averaged beams from planet observations by the SATs. Measuring the telescope beam response at different frequencies across the observing bands enables modeling the system's frequency-dependent behavior. This helps track optical non-idealities. The comparison with planet beams informs the frequency resolution necessary to accurately reconstruct the band-averaged beams in this way; it uses only the average drone and planet products, as it is intended to demonstrate the feasibility of the frequency-resolved calibration scheme rather than to set the precise beam covariance and instrument requirements. We find that the beams of the two SATs near 90 GHz follow the frequency scaling expected for diffraction-limited optics, with only modest deviations observed in the nearest lobes of one telescope. We establish consistency between the real band-averaged planet beams and the synthesized drone band-averaged beams for the center wafers of both telescopes, with an average deviation smaller than 4% for multipoles $\ell < 500$.

papers.title: Deep learning methods for gamma event selection in TAIGA-IACT image analysis in stereo-mode
papers.abstract: In astrophysical complex TAIGA there are four Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs), located at a distance of 300-500 m from each other, due to which extensive air showers (EAS) generated by cosmic and gamma radiation are recorded by a single telescope or by multiple telescopes simultaneously (stereo-mode). The analysis of EAS images from two or more Cherenkov telescopes together is of particular interest, since for this approach the reconstruction of physical parameters of the primary gamma ray is much more accurate than in mono-observations. However, the gamma-ray event reconstruction strongly depends on the quality of the hadron background suppression of the classifier, therefore, the gamma event selection stage is one of the important ones in the further analysis of IACT data. We propose and study several neural network methods for gamma event selection in joint TAIGA-IACT image analysis. Neural network methods we suggested involves a single-stage analysis of IACT images from two telescopes, while the second method considers the formation of autoencoder-derived essential features that contain the EAS physical parameters, including the type of primary particle.

papers.title: Institutional broadening of the Japanese astronomy and astrophysics research community during 1996-2025
papers.abstract: Using bibliometric data from publication records, we investigate the institutional broadening of Japanese astronomy and astrophysics over 1996-2025. The number of Japan-affiliated publications increased from 588 to 2,156, and the number of unique participating Japanese institutions increased from 123 to 227, indicating a nominal broadening of the institutional base. However, institution-publication links remained concentrated among leading institutions, and the effective number of institutions, a frequency-weighted diversity measure, increased more gradually than the number of unique participating institutions. These results show that Japanese astronomy and astrophysics broadened institutionally, but not through a complete equalization of institutional participation. The observed change is best interpreted as an expansion of the participating institutional base around a persistent core of leading institutions.

papers.title: Initial Performance Tests of MASTA for Wide-Field Narrowband Imaging
papers.abstract: Wide-field narrowband imaging provides an efficient approach for mapping low-surface-brightness line emission over large angular scales. We present initial performance tests of Multi-Application Survey Telescope Array (MASTA) for narrowband imaging. Using commissioning data obtained with the QHY461 and COSMOS-8K cameras, we characterize the basic reduction procedure, photometric calibration, image quality, and point-source detection limits. The measured surface-brightness and point-source detection limits become deeper with increasing exposure time, roughly following the expected background-limited scaling. Under the current observing and reduction conditions, the COSMOS-8K camera generally reaches deeper surface-brightness limits, particularly in the red filters, while QHY461 has smaller pixel size and provides better sampling of the telescope point spread function (PSF). As demonstrations, we perform continuum subtraction for the nearby galaxy M106 and the supernova remnant Cygnus Loop using adjacent narrowband filters and reveal the H{\alpha} and [O III] structures in M106 and filamentary structures in the Cygnus Loop. We further compare the MASTA surface brightness H{\alpha} map of M106 with an independent SITELLE measurement. After accounting for [N II] contamination and the wavelength-dependent response of the 6544 {\AA} filter in the f /1.7 converging beam, the corrected median ratio is 0.973. These tests indicate that MASTA is a promising facility for wide-field narrowband imaging. Further improvements in calibration frames, including flux calibration, field-dependent bandpass characterization, and spatially varying PSF modeling and matching will be required for quantitative studies of diffuse ionized gas.

papers.title: Extinction by non-spherical particles with the Nanoparticle Transition Matrix Code: perspectives for interstellar medium and exoplanetary atmospheres
papers.abstract: The Transition Matrix formalism (T-matrix) offers an optimal solution to the problem of radiation scattering and absorption by particles characterized by a high degree of chemical and structural complexity. However, its application to particle models composed by large numbers of constituents has been classically limited by the substantial computational burden of the method. As a consequence, the investigation of light scattering and absorption processes, in cases where particle asymmetry and non-homogeneity play an important role, typically need to rely on simplifying assumptions which affect the correct interpretation of transmission spectra and extinction curves. This problem has a huge impact on many fields of scientific application. In particular, it has a critical role in astrophysics, because the ability to model highly non homogeneous particles is a fundamental requirement to understand the role of extinction in different phases of the interstellar medium (ISM), as well as to probe the physics of light transmission in planetary atmospheres within the Solar System and beyond. In this work we describe the application of a new implementation of the T-matrix formalism, based on the framework originally developed by Borghese, Denti & Saija and named Nano-particle Transition Matrix code, which leverages the power of modern hardware architectures to reduce the computational costs related to the solution of relevant particle models for the investigation of dust in the ISM and of hot-Jupyter class planets atmospheric aerosols. This new implementation of the T-matrix formalism can handle calculations of increasing complexity with a direct impact in the interpretation of the transmission spectra of transiting exoplanets produced by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and of those expected from the Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large survey (ARIEL).

papers.title: OASIS: On-the-fly ASynchronous Image Stream classification -- Transformer-based models for the early detection of strongly lensed supernovae
papers.abstract: Time-domain surveys often produce asynchronous image sequences across irregular observation times and photometric bands. In many applications, predictions are needed after each new observation, particularly when transient sources must be identified early to trigger follow-up. Strongly lensed supernovae (LSNe), for which follow-up is particularly time-critical, provide a useful example. We formulate this setting as On-the-fly ASynchronous Image Stream (OASIS) classification and explore reusable transformer architectures for causal, on-the-fly classification. We demonstrate these architectures on the lensed-transient classification problem studied by Bag et al. (2026a,b), distinguishing LSNe Ia from unlensed astrophysical transients. We compare them with the recurrent baseline adopted by Bag et al. (2026b), which combines a ConvLSTM branch for image processing with a separate LSTM branch for encoding observation times. The baseline maps asynchronous observations onto a fixed band-by-observation grid, filling unobserved bands with zeros. Using a common training setup, we compare two transformer-based approaches to modeling interactions among spatio-temporal tokens: factorized attention, which separates spatial and temporal interactions, and joint attention, which models them together. On the demonstration dataset, factorized architectures achieve mean losses of $0.095$--$0.100$, compared with $0.128$ for the recurrent baseline and $0.107$ or higher for joint architectures. A selective readout further reduces the best loss to $0.089$ for a factorized model. These results suggest that factorized attention suits this dataset better, without implying universal architectural superiority. We release the architectures as reusable foundations for time-domain astronomy and other applications involving evolving spatial features that require on-the-fly predictions.

papers.title: Estimating the spectral resolution of a radio data cube from its noise properties
papers.abstract: We present a new method to estimate the spectral resolution of a radio data cube from its noise properties. We assume that the data cube is the result of the convolution of a spectrally-uncorrelated cube with a constant convolution kernel K. We demonstrate that K and the resolution, defined as K's integral, can be estimated thanks to the analytical relation between the autocorrelation of the noise spectra extracted from the cube and the power spectrum of the kernel. We discuss a number of algorithms that make this method robust in the realistic case of a finite number of spectra and channels, real signal and artefacts, and we present the results obtained for a number of datasets from the literature. We further highlight that this method is applicable to any data cube that meets our assumptions independently of the observing frequency or the exact nature of the cube's "third" axis, e.g., it could be used to measure the time resolution of transient-search data cubes. We make this method available as part of the open-source software tool spectre.

papers.title: Graph Learning with Multiplicative Aggregation for Solar Filament Fragment Association Modeling in Full-disk H$\alpha$ Images
papers.abstract: Solar filaments are prominent features in H$\alpha$ observations. During their evolution, they often exhibit complex morphological and topological changes, which, due to line-of-sight projection effects, appear as fragmentation and merging. These phenomena make it difficult to reliably track solar filaments using automated methods, as the same structure may appear different over time. To address this issue, we formulate filament fragment association as a graph-based learning problem, where individual fragments are represented as nodes and candidate pairwise relationships are modeled as edges to infer whether fragments belong to the same filament. Furthermore, we propose a novel graph neural network (GNN) that incorporates multiplicative aggregation layers to enhance feature aggregation in the graph, replacing conventional additive aggregation with a multiplicative mechanism to better capture information between fragments. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves reliable performance in filament fragment association, validating the effectiveness of the graph-based formulation and the proposed multiplicative aggregation mechanism.

papers.title: Simulation and Deep Learning Inversion for Full-sky Energetic Neutral Atom Imaging at the Heliospheric Boundary
papers.abstract: The distribution of energetic neutral atom (ENA) differential flux density at the heliospheric boundary is the key to revealing the interaction mechanism between the solar wind and the interstellar medium. The Helios ENA Rapid Mapper (HERMA) is a pre-research project for a new ENA detection concept and technical principle, which is designed to provide technical support for refined detection with its advantages of wide energy range coverage and high spatial resolution. To verify the high spatiotemporal resolution rapid imaging capability of the HERMA, this study restored the particle response characteristics of the HERMA (spatial modulation grid + 256-pixel linear array silicon detector) based on Geant4 simulation, and we compared the performance of the traditional inversion algorithm with the convolutional neural network (CNN) inversion algorithm using INCA data as the benchmark. The results show that under different sampling times, the source distribution inverted by the CNN algorithm has a higher degree of agreement with the ideally expected distribution, and the CNN algorithm exhibits better stability and accuracy than the traditional algorithm under the conditions of low signal-to-noise ratio and short staring time. This study provides core technical support for the engineering verification and on-orbit application of the HERMA instrument, fills the technical gap in wide-energy-range and high-resolution ENA detection, and helps to deepen the research on the interaction mechanism between the solar wind and the interstellar medium at the heliospheric boundary.

papers.title: Charge Response Simulation of Liquid Argon Compton Cameras for Precise MeV Gamma-Ray Event Reconstruction
papers.abstract: We studied the detector response for a liquid-argon time-projection chamber (LArTPC) Compton camera targeting MeV gamma-ray astronomy by a Geant4-based Monte Carlo simulation. The simulation, implemented within ComptonSoft, incorporates electron-ion recombination, charge diffusion, and induction on the electrode pixels. We evaluated the angular resolution measure (ARM) and the energy reconstruction error as functions of electronic noise, pixel pitch, and the recombination correction method. An electronic noise level of 4 keV and a pixel pitch of 1 mm yield an ARM (FWHM) of about 3 degrees at 1332.5 keV and an energy reconstruction error better than 4\% for incident energies of 1173.2 keV and above. Recombination correction using both scintillation light and charge signals improves the ARM and the energy error by factors of 1.7--2.3 and 2.2--5.4, respectively, compared to the charge-only correction, although the uncertainty of the recombination-fluctuation model remains. Since this simulation relies on idealized assumptions such as the use of the Monte Carlo truth in the event reconstruction, these values represent the best cases achievable under these detector conditions; nevertheless, they show that a large-scale LArTPC is a promising Compton camera for cosmic MeV gamma-ray observations.

papers.title: Ushering in high angular resolution observatories in the far-infrared: The case for a double-Fourier interferometer
papers.abstract: A far-infrared (far-IR) interferometer from a space-based platform would bring about a transformational improvement in the spatial detail of astronomical observations that are inaccessible from ground-based observatories. This orders-of-magnitude improvement would significantly advance studies of newly formed and mature exoplanetary systems and their potential for supporting life, the earliest stages of star formation, and the evolution of galaxies up to the peak of the Universe's star formation activity and beyond. In this work, we discuss the potential for such an instrument and the science it enables in complement to current long-term plans of the global astronomical community and in preparation for the next generation of observatories. We also outline notable far-IR mission concepts, pathfinder instruments, and technology development platforms that have been studied and developed throughout the past few decades and briefly discuss key enabling technologies.

papers.title: Establishing baseline model performances for optical turbulence forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting of optical turbulence (OT) is useful to optimise telescope scheduling and maximising observing efficiency, as the performance of adaptive optics systems strongly depends on turbulence conditions. While various numerical weather prediction and machine learning models are developed to predict these complex turbulence properties, properly evaluating their added value requires well-defined baseline reference models. This study establishes baseline performance thresholds for key astroclimatic parameters using two distinct models: one forecasting the parameter average over a specific timescale, and the other forecasting the temporal evolution over the same specific timescale. We apply these frameworks to extensive, multi-year datasets from the sites of the Very Large Telescope (VLT) and the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT) and discuss the possibility of extrapolating reference values of forecast performances for other sites based on their optical turbulence statistical characteristics. Our results show that baseline predictive accuracy varies according to the observing site, the specific parameter, the chosen timescale, and the forecasting approach. Therefore, an OT forecasting model's accuracy cannot be quantified in absolute terms, but relatively to the baseline.

papers.title: TESS Pulsation Timing Reveals the JWST Calibration Star HD 158485 as a Double-pulsator Binary
papers.abstract: HD~158485 is an A-type $\delta$~Scuti star in the CALSPEC network and the JWST absolute-flux calibration program. Gaia DR3 assigns it a binary classification probability close to unity but provides no orbital solution. Using TESS observations from Sectors 14--26, 40--41, 47--60, and 73--86, we measure the pulsation phases of six $\delta$~Scuti modes. The frequencies form two groups with opposite light-travel-time delays, revealing two pulsating components. A direct light-curve forward model yields an orbital period of $P_{\rm orb}=382.80^{+0.80}_{-0.76}$~d, eccentricity $e=0.242^{+0.045}_{-0.046}$, projected light-time amplitudes of $195.8^{+9.2}_{-8.9}$ and $239.7^{+6.8}_{-6.8}$~s, and a dynamical mass ratio of $q=M_B/M_A=0.818^{+0.046}_{-0.045}$. A blind prediction based only on the first two long TESS campaigns reproduces the third campaign without updating the orbital parameters, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of $r=0.983$. Its held-out rms is 83.8~s, compared with 289.9~s when the period is fixed at 365.25~d. A 5.15-$\sigma$ Hipparcos--Gaia EDR3 proper-motion anomaly independently indicates unresolved astrometric motion. The unresolved companion can also affect spectrophotometric predictions: a conditional PB2-constrained two-atmosphere model differs from the corresponding single-star atmosphere prediction by 1.6\% over 1--5~$\mu$m and 2.5\% over 5--28~$\mu$m. HD~158485 therefore shows that a calibration-relevant binary can lack a catalogued orbital solution while two independent pulsation clocks reveal and measure its orbit.

papers.title: The $R$-Process Alliance: On J0010$-$1735, an Accreted, Chemically Unusual, Metal-poor Star with $R$-process Enhancement
papers.abstract: We present a detailed chemo-dynamical analysis of the chemically peculiar very metal-poor ([Fe/H]$=-2.22\pm 0.11$) Milky Way (MW) halo star, 2MASS J00101758$-$1735387 (hereafter J0010-1735), discovered by the $R$-Process Alliance. We derive abundances for 45 elements, including 28 neutron-capture elements, and confirm that \thestar\ is highly $r$-process-enhanced, with [Eu/Fe]=$+1.30$. The light, $\alpha$, and Fe-peak element abundances ratios relative to Fe are all sub-solar, aside from C, Si, and most extremely, Ca. We investigate three possible formation scenarios based on the star's chemical abundances and orbital kinematics: whether it formed in the \textit{in-situ} MW halo, in a MW dwarf galaxy satellite, or in a satellite of the Magellanic Cloud system. Using the position of \thestar\ in the [Mg/Mn]--[Al/Fe] plane, the abundance pattern of both the light and heavy elements, and the kinematics, we conclude that J0010-1735 most plausibly originated in a now-disrupted ultra-faint dwarf galaxy that was accreted into the MW halo. We examine potential chemical enrichment scenarios of J0010-1735, including one similar to the $r$-process-enhanced UFD Reticulum II, or enrichment via a sub-Chandrasekhar Type Ia SNe, potentially supplemented by a Ca-rich gap transient and by a separate neutron-rich site that facilitated $r$-process enrichment. A nuclear cosmochronometric age of $12.5\pm4.2$ Gyr is derived from the [Th/Eu] ratio, consistent with an ancient origin in one of the earliest star-forming systems in the universe.

papers.title: Radial increase of the compensated interplanetary magnetic field magnitude as a result of the growth of spherically polarized Alfv\'en waves
papers.abstract: Measurements from the NASA Parker Solar Probe (PSP) mission demonstrate that inside $\sim20$ solar radii ($\Rs$) the magnitude of the interplanetary magnetic field does not fall off simply as $1/R^2$, with $\avg{|B|}\,R^2$ 15--20\% below its value at $\sim60\,\Rs$. Here we use PSP magnetic field measurements over $10.6$--$56.8\,\Rs$ to show that the outward rise of $\avg{|B|}\,R^2$ is not due to the global structure of the heliospheric magnetic field or proximity to the heliospheric current sheet but is the direct result of the growth of large-amplitude, spherically polarized Alfv\'en waves (so-called `switchbacks'). Over the same distance range, $\avg{B_R}\,R^2$ stays constant, so that the sector-signed radial flux is conserved. The wave amplitude $\epsilon = B_{\perp,{\rm rms}}/\avg{B_\parallel}$ grows from $0.26$ to $0.57$ as $R^{1/2}\cos\alpha$, and $\avg{|B|}/\avg{B_R}$ rises by $20\%$. A simple model parametrized by the broadening of the distribution of deflection angles reproduces the effect to high accuracy. These results demonstrate that as the relative wave amplitudes grow with increasing solar distance, a dynamo-like process operates to enhance the field magnitude by up to $20\%$. By enhancing magnetic pressure this has implications for the large scale solar wind structure in the low-beta inner heliosphere, as well as partially resolving the long-standing discrepancy between remote measurements of the solar magnetic field and those made in situ by earlier missions farther from the Sun.

papers.title: Integration of a CME Flux Rope Model with Magnetic Field Draping in Heliospheric Simulations
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of the magnetic structure of interplanetary coronal mass ejections (ICMEs) remains a key challenge in space weather forecasting. Despite several efforts using global MHD modeling, it remains difficult to deduce a flux-rope solution that can accurately and reliably reproduce the magnetic structure of a CME. We present FROST (Flux Rope embedded in the Solar Magnetic Field), a new flux-rope model implementation within the European Heliospheric Forecast Information Asset (EUHFORIA), featuring an initially force-free toroidal flux rope embedded in the low-coronal magnetic field. FROST employs a novel embedding technique that self-consistently generates a draping magnetic field around the flux-rope, ensuring continuity of the normal magnetic field component at the CME boundary. The dynamics of the flux-rope in the low and middle corona is solved by a non-uniform advection constrained by the observed kinematics of the event. This results in a global, non-toroidal, stretched loop-like magnetic structure. At heliospheric distances, the evolution is modeled as an MHD process using EUHFORIA. We validate the FROST model implementation by simulating the CME event of 2013 April 11 and comparing the results with in situ magnetic field measurements at 1 au. The modeled magnetic field profiles of the flux-rope exhibit strong agreement with the observations, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.64-0.93 for Bx, 0.92-0.95 for By, and 0.82-0.87 for Bz component of the magnetic field. These results demonstrate the capability of the proposed flux-rope model to significantly improve ICME magnetic field prediction, highlighting its strong potential for advancing space-weather forecasting capabilities.

papers.title: Grand minima and intermittency in near-critical convection-driven dynamos
papers.abstract: Context: Solar magnetism exhibits long-term variations on timescales of decades to centuries. Aims: The main aim is to study how the supercriticality of the dynamo affects the variability of magnetic fields on timescales relevant to the Sun. Methods: Three-dimensional rotating magnetohydrodynamic simulations in a spherical wedge geometry are used to produce self-consistent convection-driven dynamos. The supercriticality of the dynamo is controlled by varying the magnetic diffusivity. Results: The main result is that long-term variability of the dynamo increases with decreasing supercriticality of the dynamo and that cases nearest to the onset of dynamo action show extended grand minima-like periods of low activity. The simulations fall in three classes where the least supercritical cases show the largest variations of magnetic activity and where the flow including differential rotation is almost unaffected by the magnetic field. In the cases with the highest supercriticality the magnetic field is permanently strong and differential rotation permanently quenched, both having relatively little temporal variation. In an intermediate regime both the magnetic fields and differential rotation exhibit strong anticorrelated fluctuations. Conclusions: The occurrence of grand minima in the Sun has been conjectured to be due to a weakly supercritical dynamo. The current results support this idea and suggest that the absence of grand minima in earlier global dynamo simulations is because their large-scale dynamos were too supercritical. Furthermore, the current results suggest that the effect of the magnetic field on differential rotation is negligible if the average rms-field is less than about 2~kG.

papers.title: From the QBO to Rieger-type periods: Explaining extreme solar events by tidally triggered magneto-Rossby waves
papers.abstract: It has recently been demonstrated that the occurrence of extreme solar events is governed by a phase-stable period close to 1.723 years (629.29 days). According to our previously developed tidally-synchronized solar dynamo model, this is one of the periods resulting from two-planet spring tides exerted by the tidally dominant planets Venus, Earth and Jupiter, which trigger magneto-Rossby waves in the solar tachocline. Overall, the squared sum of these three waves incorporates nine periods ranging from 59 to 629 days. Using a standard Rayleigh test, we demonstrate that all nine of these periods can be identified in the data on extreme solar events. For the latter, we use a combination of 72 ground-level enhancement (GLE) events with various X-flare data, the number of which increases when the threshold is successively lowered from X10 to X1. To identify the spectral peaks, it is necessary to analyze the sidebands that emerge due to the modulation with the longer-term periods such as the 11-year Schwabe cycle and the third harmonics of the Hale cycle. In this framework, the seminal Rieger period of 154 days is re-interpreted as the lower sideband of 146 days which is the quarter of the synodic period of Venus and Earth.

papers.title: SiO Maser Line-width Diagnostics of AGB Stars and Red Supergiants: The RSG-adjacent Region in the FWZI--Luminosity Plane
papers.abstract: We investigate whether SiO maser line profiles can distinguish asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars from red supergiants (RSGs) and identify unusual AGB-classified sources near the RSG regime. We compiled 2,956 detected SiO maser spectra for 1,551 objects and constructed reference samples of 1,068 O-rich AGB stars and 36 RSGs. The full width at zero intensity (FWZI) was reliably measured for 1,020 AGB stars and 32 RSGs. AGB stars are concentrated at narrow line widths: 81.5% have FWZI <10 km s^-1, whereas 81.2% of RSGs have FWZI >15 km s^-1 and none has FWZI <10 km s^-1. Infrared two-color diagrams provide only partial separation. Combining FWZI with luminosities based primarily on quality-filtered Gaia/Bailer-Jones distances, with independent literature distances for several RSGs, reveals a weak tendency for wider SiO maser lines at higher luminosities but no clean boundary. We therefore define an empirical RSG-adjacent region in the FWZI-luminosity plane, 15 <= FWZI <= 26.6 km s^-1 and 3.9 <= log(L/L_sun) <= 4.9, to characterize the high-luminosity, broad-line tail of the AGB-classified sample. Ten sources fall within this region.
